title: Dedicated Capacity Discovery - Lakemont Financial
next_steps: Send Dedicated capacity pricing and commitment tiers
Share SOC 2 / security pack and KMS integration notes
Schedule a 2-hour performance benchmark next week with sample traffic
action_items: Jared - send pricing and reserved GPU options by 2026-03-06
Priya - prepare benchmark plan + sample config and share by 2026-03-07
Daniel - provide current traffic pattern CSV and peak RPS by 2026-03-05
summary: Discovery focused on Dedicated (reserved GPUs) for Lakemont's customer-facing NLU and chat use cases; requirements: data isolation, VPC, predictable latency with burst capability for month-end loads. Agreed to run benchmarks and share pricing and security docs. SE to propose autoscale/burst approach and pilot plan.
transcript:
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jared from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. Priya our solutions engineer is here too. Uh, quick intros?
[00:12] Mark: Hi, Mark Reynolds, head of ML at Lakemont. We've got Sara, our CTO, and Daniel who runs infra.
[00:20] Priya: Hi all, thanks. we'll keep this focused on Dedicated capacity questions, isolation, and how burst works.
[00:29] Sara: Yeah, we want to understand tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated; security is a big deal for us, and month-end spikes are a pain.
[00:38] Jared: Totally. Real quick, can you give a sense of current stack and what you're serving? models, throughput, that kind of thing.
[00:46] Mark: Sure. Primary is customer support triage and automated responses - a mix of retrieval-augmented generation and NLU classifiers. We currently run models in-house on mixed GPU fleet, mostly 8 A100-ish nodes right now, but it's a mess. Typical steady-state is ~150 qps for embeddings/candidates, peaks up to 900 qps during statement cycles.
[01:10] Daniel: our infra runs in AWS in a VPC, we need private networking, no public endpoints for inference. Also strict KMS usage and SAML SSO, SOC2 compliance.
[01:21] Priya: Ok, got it. So isolation + VPC + KMS - sounds like Redwood Private might be a fit, but Dedicated can also meet isolation with dedicated pools and private networking.
[01:31] Sara: What's the difference operationally? We want predictable latency and cost.
[01:36] Priya: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for you, so you get predictable throughput and model pinning. You still talk to Redwood's control plane but we can offer a private endpoint inside your VPC for egress control. Private (on-prem/VPC-managed) is more isolated - you host the control plane. But Dedicated gives the compute isolation with simpler ops.
[01:57] Mark: And compliance? We need audit logs, retention, and to bring our own KMS/HSM.
[02:04] Jared: We support customer-managed KMS integrations and audit logs; we'll share SOC2 docs. Priya, can you expand on auth and RBAC?
[02:11] Priya: Sure - we integrate with SAML for SSO and have RBAC for routes and model-level access. Audit logs are exportable to your SIEM. There may be small differences in retention if you're on hosted vs private but we'll put those in the security pack.
[02:26] Daniel: How do you handle bursts? Our month-end peaks are short but intense. If we reserve 8 GPUs and suddenly need 32 for a burst how does that work?
[02:36] Priya: Two options: reserved capacity with burst credits/burst pools - you can configure allowed burst up to a cap, which spins up extra nodes from a shared pool, or autoscale with pre-warmed instances if you prefer predictability. There's a cost tradeoff: burst is cheaper for occasional spikes vs paying for constant reserved capacity.
[02:55] Mark: Do you throttle or queue requests when capacity is maxed? We can't have long tail latency.
[03:01] Priya: We do smart routing and can route to a lower-cost but higher-latency model variant as fallback; also prefix/KV cache helps for repeated patterns. For strict p99 latency SLOs, we recommend a mix: keep enough reserved to cover p95 and allow controlled burst for p99.
[03:22] Sara: What's the quantization story? We need to run some medium-size LLMs, cost matters.
[03:28] Priya: We support quantized variants and can test 8-bit/4-bit quantization. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations per workload. For Dedicated we can run both FP16 and quantized models depending on accuracy requirements.
[03:41] Mark: Are kernels optimized for our hardware? We run on NVIDIA across the fleet.
[03:46] Priya: Our runtime picks kernels based on model arch and hardware; we do assembly-level optimizations and sequence-length aware scheduling.
[03:53] Daniel: On the networking side, will traffic stay inside our VPC? We need no egress to public internet for inference payloads.
[03:59] Jared: Yes, for Dedicated we can provision private endpoints into your VPC - traffic stays inside. For Private deployments you host everything and it's entirely under your network.
[04:11] Mark: Great. We're also evaluating latency targets - we want <80ms median and <250ms p99 for chat flows at 8k context. Is that feasible?
[04:20] Priya: That depends on model size, batch strategy, and KV usage. For smaller context and optimized models we hit those numbers; at 8k context p99 of 250ms is challenging but achievable with right batching and pre-warmed KV caches. We'll need to bench with your prompt shapes.
[04:38] Sara: What data residency options do you have? We have EU customers.
[04:42] Jared: We have region routing and can pin capacity to regions; Dedicated can be launched in EU region - data residency controls apply. We'll include region availability in the pricing doc.
[04:53] Mark: On outages, what's SLA and fallback? We need graceful degradation.
[04:58] Priya: We offer SLA-backed dedicated capacity. For graceful degradation we use automatic fallback to compatible model variants or route to another region or to hosted with redaction if necessary.
[05:09] Sara: Cost model - how do you price Dedicated vs Hosted?
[05:13] Jared: Dedicated is typically monthly reserved GPU commitments with tiers; Hosted is usage-based. We'll send a tiered pricing sheet showing reserved GPU options, burst costs, and overage rates.
[05:25] Daniel: For benchmarks, what do you need from us?
[05:29] Priya: Sample traffic patterns (CSV with timestamps, request sizes), top prompts, and SLO targets. We'll propose a 2-hour bench where we replay realistic traffic and measure latency and cost.
[05:37] Mark: We're about a month out from budget sign-off; timeline is Q2 pilot if numbers look right.
[05:42] Jared: Ok, good. For pilot, we'll suggest a minimal reserved footprint + burst for peak testing.
[05:48] Sara: Any gotchas in templated deployments? e.g., data retention, logs stored in Redwood, or do you stream to our S3?
[05:56] Priya: Logs can be streamed to your S3 or SIEM; we also keep operational logs for debugging, retention negotiable. We'll call out what stays with Redwood and what you export.
[06:07] Daniel: Security review - we'll need the SOC 2 report and software SBOM.
[06:12] Jared: We'll attach SOC 2 and SBOM as part of the security pack.
[06:16] Mark: Are there customers in finance using Dedicated?
[06:19] Jared: Yes, a number - we'll share anonymized references and a short case study.
[06:24] Sara: Ok, next steps?
[06:26] Jared: Recap - Jared sends pricing and availability; Priya shares benchmark plan; Daniel sends traffic CSV; schedule bench next week. Anything else?
[06:36] Mark: Also need proof of encryption at rest with BYOK/KMS and logging retention details.
[06:40] Priya: We'll include KMS integration steps and retention matrix in the pack.
[06:44] Sara: Sound good. Thanks everyone.
[06:46] Jared: Thanks - we'll follow up with the docs and get the bench on calendar.
[06:50] (call ends)

Notes: transcript includes small transcription artifacts (e.g., K-V cash instead of KV cache in a couple lines), filler words, and speaker overlaps.
